You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From a434e2398ae9ac5ccf3ec5ec7d50638a38ae95f6 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Karel Zak <kzak@redhat.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2015 09:53:46 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] raw: fix raw query

Bug introduced by commit cd121363.

References: https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1181444
Signed-off-by: Karel Zak <kzak@redhat.com>
---
 disk-utils/raw.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/disk-utils/raw.c b/disk-utils/raw.c
index cc6690145..d29ff1ba3 100644
--- a/disk-utils/raw.c
+++ b/disk-utils/raw.c
@@ -224,7 +224,7 @@ static int query(int minor_raw, const char *raw_name, int quiet)
 	if (raw_name) {
 		struct stat statbuf;
 
-		if (!stat(raw_name, &statbuf))
+		if (stat(raw_name, &statbuf) != 0)
 			err(EXIT_RAW_ACCESS,
 			    _("Cannot locate raw device '%s'"), raw_name);
 		if (!S_ISCHR(statbuf.st_mode))
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was introduced by incorrect logic in the condition checking the result of the `stat` function. The original code incorrectly continued execution and reported an error when `stat` succeeded (returned 0), which would lead to erroneous behavior when trying to locate a raw device. The condition was fixed to check for a failure (when `stat` returns a non-zero value), ensuring that an error is reported correctly only when the raw device does not exist.

Root cause:
The bug was introduced by incorrect logic in the condition checking the result of the `stat` function. The original code incorrectly continued execution and reported an error when `stat` succeeded (returned 0), which would lead to erroneous behavior when trying to locate a raw device. The condition was fixed to check for a failure (when `stat` returns a non-zero value), ensuring that an error is reported correctly only when the raw device does not exist.
